recentItems.title: Hudson Valley News Today: Campus stabbing, Yonkers animal cruelty case and I-84 DWI crash
recentItems.description:
Authorities say two people are in custody after a stabbing near a student center left one person seriously injured and requiring surgery. recentItems.title: Man charged with attempted murder after thruway road rage shooting
recentItems.description:
A road rage confrontation on Interstate 87 escalated into gunfire and an attempted murder charge for a Yonkers man, according to police. Investigators say 28-year-old Elmy Manuel Sandoval-Firpo cut off another driver while entering a gas station on Tuckahoe Road, leading to a verbal dispute. Authorities say he later smashed the victim's rear windshield, rammed the vehicle on the New York Thruway and fired a gun at the driver. No injuries were reported. Police say Sandoval-Firpo fled, struck a Yonkers police vehicle during an attempted stop, and was arrested after his vehicle became disabled by a flat tire. He faces charges including attempted murder, attempted assault and reckless endangerment.

recentItems.title: NYPD officer arrested in $50K burglary of Bronx home
recentItems.description:
An NYPD officer is accused of using department software to obtain information that investigators say helped him break into a Bronx home and steal nearly $50,000 worth of cash, jewelry and personal documents. Authorities allege Luis Triunfel later monitored the investigation through NYPD systems and returned to the apartment complex to erase surveillance video. The officer has been suspended without pay and is facing multiple charges, including burglary and tampering with evidence.

recentItems.title: Should NYC students use fewer screens at school?
recentItems.description:
New York City Council members are debating whether public schools should place more limits on student screen time and technology use. Council leaders raised concerns about school-issued devices, YouTube access in classrooms, student data privacy and the impact of educational technology. Proposed changes include banning one-to-one devices for students in grades K through 5, limiting certain digital learning tools and expanding teacher guidance. The discussion comes as NYC Public Schools pause most AI use for students in kindergarten through eighth grade and continue evaluating technology's role in education.
